room-2-1-0.name: a Silk-Choked Bank
room-2-1-0.description:

riverbank that directly borders the steady flow of the water channel. Sticky,
milky-white webbing clings stubbornly to the low-hanging branches and coats

the shore, marking a clear trail where a massive hunger leaves the deep hollow.

room-3-3-0.name: River Running
room-3-3-0.description:
The river continues its steady, southwards journey, flowing smoothly between
low, earthen banks that show signs of gradual erosion. The water remains crisp
and relatively shallow, allowing the bright sunlight to illuminate the clean,
stony riverbed beneath the main channel. Tiny ripples disrupt the surface where
smaller fish dart between the rocks, while deep along the bottom, massive and
ancient forms glide silently through the shadows of the lower current.

room-3-4-0.name: a Clear Channel in the River Running
room-3-4-0.description:
The river straightens completely here, running in a clean, unhurried channel
between the low banks. Beneath the surface, the heavy current drops its silt,
revealing a smooth bed of light clay and flat stones well out of the sun's reach.
Faint ripples mar the water as ancient, bottom-dwelling life stirs sluggishly
through the cool depths, entirely concealed by the steady, unyielding flow of
the main channel.

room-0-5-0.name: A Nook in the Mountains
room-0-5-0.description: A narrow, rocky shelf clings to the sheer mountain face, providing a small pocket of level ground amidst the towering peaks. Jagged stone walls press in from the sides, their gray surfaces split by deep fissures where hardy alpine mosses manage to take root. Littered across the dirt floor are the cracked, hollow remains of discarded eggshells, half-buried in the scree. A sharp, distinct musk hangs heavy in the thin air, hinting at the large predators that occasionally seek shelter within this rugged alcove.

room-2-5-0.description:

higher ridges to the west. The air carries a heavy, damp stillness, characteristic
of the wild borderlands where the great lake meets the forest eaves. Sedge
and coarse river grass sprout in patches between the trees, surviving where
the woodland floor dips low and gathers the runoff from the northern plains.

room-0-6-0.name: Windswept Mountain Ridge
room-0-6-0.description:
A treacherous, exposed path winds precariously along the sun-bleached rock of
the mountain ridge. To the north, the trail dips slightly toward a sheltered
recess, while southern views reveal a gradual descent toward greener slopes.
Stunted, wind-battered shrubs claw for a foothold in the sparse soil, their
twisted branches frozen in defensive postures against the elements. Ground
predators and nimble mountain herbivores frequently cross this high thoroughfare.

room-1-6-0.name: Elevated Perch
room-1-6-0.description:
The rugged ridge ascends sharply to a high, windswept vantage point, offering
a commanding view over the lower forest canopy spreading out towards the east.
Skeletal branches of weather-beaten pine trees claw at the sky, anchoring
themselves precariously among the pale, fractured crags. Deep fissures score
the grey stone underfoot, where coarse mountain grass grows in sparse clumps
sheltered from the biting northern gales.

room-0-7-0.name: The Base of the Crags
room-0-7-0.description:
The steep mountain terrain flattens out, giving way to a broken landscape of
low, rolling hills. To the north, the massive stone ridges of the high peaks
tower dramatically against the skyline, marking a sharp contrast to the open
ground here. Patches of tough, coarse brush claw for survival among scattered
boulders that have tumbled down from the upper slopes over the centuries. A
hardy alpine breeze sweeps across the expanse, carrying the faint scent of pine.

room-0-8-0.name: a Jagged Crag
room-0-8-0.description:
Scattered boulders and splintered branches choke this narrow, rocky hollow,
where the mountain terrain transitions into the low hills. A murky, stagnant
pond is nestled tightly between old roots, its dark water reflecting the grim
cliffs above. High overhead, wide thermal currents trace the sky, watched by
distant, unseen eyes waiting for signs of weakness below. Fresh, heavy tracks
deep in the soft mud along the water's edge give clear warning of what roams.

The ASCIIMAP is the "root" map we use for all building projects. This map
directly informs the "sector" of each room.


Key
===

. = field or brush
~ = river or water
t = trail through field or brush
f = forest
( = forested hills
[ = barren/grass/brush hills
> = mountains

lore.body: This region lies just south of Esgaroth (Long Lake) and east of the dark eaves of Mirkwood, where the River Running (Celduin) flows south toward the Sea of Rhûn. Historically, this area serves as a vital trade corridor where the Raft-men of Thranduil's realm, the Men of Dale, and the merchants of Dorwinion interact. The presence of the Dorwinion Road highlights its role as a bustling mercantile highway, though its proximity to the wild edges of Mirkwood leaves it vulnerable to stray orcs, spiders, and bandits preying on wealthy wine caravans.
